# Changelog

The full history is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/s00d/onlinesim-js-api/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

## 2.1.1

- Fixed types against the current API: `Profile.number`/`country`, optional `Operation.response`, `RentSms.code` `0` for `notify` SMS, nullable free-list and payment fields; `paymentHistory().paylist` is kept when it arrives as a list.
- `waitCode` retries `TRY_AGAIN_LATER` (rate limit), `ERROR_UNDEFINED` and `INTERVAL_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_ERROR`.
- `MockOnlineSim` follows the backend more closely: rent reservation and confirmation, `setOperationRevise` and `closeRentNum` answers, missing vs wrong key — see [Testing](https://s00d.github.io/onlinesim-js-api/testing).

## 2.1.0

- New: `MockOnlineSim`, an offline fake of the API for your tests — see [Testing](https://s00d.github.io/onlinesim-js-api/testing).
- `exports` includes `"./package.json"`; the package ships `CHANGELOG.md`.

## 2.0.0

A rewrite with a new API; v1 code does not run unchanged.

- One client, `new OnlineSim({ apiKey })`, with the sections as properties: `client.numbers`, `client.rent`, `client.user`, `client.free`.
- Zero runtime dependencies (global `fetch`, Node.js 18+), ESM + CommonJS + types.
- The key is sent as a Bearer header, never in the URL.
- Typed errors: `ApiError`, `NoNumberError`, `TransportError`, `TimeoutError`.
- `numbers.waitCode` replaces `wait_code`: real interval and timeout, `keepOpen`, `since`, retries network errors.
- `rent.get` creates extendable rents by default (`extension = true`).
- New: `user.setWebhookUrl` / `clearWebhookUrl` / `webhookLogs`, `parseWebhook`.
- Removed: the proxy API, `onlineProxy`, `numbers.repeat`, `numbers.service`, `numbers.serviceNumber`, `rent.portReload`, `user.createEmpty`, `free.countries` / `numbers` / `messages` (use `free.list`).


# Free numbers

## list

Countries, the numbers of the selected country and the SMS of the selected number, in one call.

```ts
list(options?: { country?: number; number?: string; page?: number; count?: number }): Promise<FreeList>
```

| Option    | Type     | Default        | Description                                                     |
| --------- | -------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `country` | `number` | `44` (server)  | Country code; an unknown one falls back to the first available. |
| `number`  | `string` | first number   | Number **without** the country code, as the keys of `numbers`.  |
| `page`    | `number` | `1`            | Page of `messages`.                                             |
| `count`   | `number` | server default | SMS per page, 10–500.                                           |

`FreeList`:

- `countries`: `{ country, country_text, country_original }[]`
- `numbers`: `Record<string, { country, country_original, full_number, data_humans, is_archive }>`, keyed by the short number
- `messages`: a paginator of `{ id, text, in_number, my_number, code, created_at, data_humans }` plus `number` and `country`; `code` is `-` when no code was found

```ts
const { numbers } = await client.free.list({ country: 44 })
const short = Object.keys(numbers)[0]
if (short) {
  const { messages } = await client.free.list({ country: 44, number: short, count: 20 })
  for (const sms of messages.data) console.log(sms.in_number, sms.code, sms.text)
}
```


# Numbers

An operation (`tzid`) is one ordered number. Order it with `get`/`getWithNumber`, read the SMS with `stateOne` or `waitCode`, finish it with `close` (or `ban`). Countries are phone codes (`7`, `44`, …), services are slugs (`google`, `vkcom`, …) as returned by `tariffs`.

## price

Price of one number, USD; `null` when the country has no price for the service.

```ts
price(service: string, country = 7): Promise<number | null>
```

| Param     | Type     | Default | Description   |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ------------- |
| `service` | `string` | —       | Service slug. |
| `country` | `number` | `7`     | Country code. |

```ts
const usd = await client.numbers.price('google', 44)
```

Errors: `ApiError` `ERROR_NO_SERVICE`, `UNDEFINED_COUNTRY`.

## get

Order a number; returns the operation id. Freezes the price on the balance.

```ts
get(service: string, country = 7, options?: { reject?: Array<string | number> }): Promise<number>
```

| Param            | Type                     | Default      | Description                               |
| ---------------- | ------------------------ | ------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `service`        | `string`                 | —            | Service slug.                             |
| `country`        | `number`                 | `7`          | Country code.                             |
| `options.reject` | `Array<string | number>` | profile list | Number prefixes to skip, e.g. `['4470']`. |

```ts
const tzid = await client.numbers.get('google', 44, { reject: ['4470'] })
```

Errors: `NoNumberError`; `ApiError` `WARNING_LOW_BALANCE`, `ERROR_NO_SERVICE`, `UNDEFINED_COUNTRY`, `EXCEEDED_CONCURRENT_OPERATIONS`, `INTERVAL_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_ERROR`, `TRY_AGAIN_LATER`.

## getWithNumber

Same as `get`, but returns the number right away.

```ts
getWithNumber(service: string, country = 7, options?: { reject?: Array<string | number> }): Promise<NumberOrder>
```

Returns `NumberOrder`: `{ tzid, number, country, time, service, title?, guard_interval_remaining_seconds? }` — `number` with `+`, `time` in seconds left.

```ts
const { tzid, number } = await client.numbers.getWithNumber('google', 44)
```

Errors: as `get`.

## state

All operations of the account; `[]` when there are none.

```ts
state(options?: { messageToCode?: boolean; orderBy?: 'asc' | 'desc'; msgList?: boolean }): Promise<Operation[]>
```

| Option          | Type             | Default | Description                                          |
| --------------- | ---------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `messageToCode` | `boolean`        | `true`  | `msg` is the code only; `false` — the full SMS text. |
| `orderBy`       | `'asc' | 'desc'` | `'asc'` | Order of operations.                                 |
| `msgList`       | `boolean`        | `false` | `msg` is a list of all SMS (`OperationSms[]`).       |

`Operation`: `{ tzid, response, number?, service?, country?, sum?, time?, msg?, guard_interval_remaining_seconds?, … }`.
`response` is the state: `TZ_INPOOL` (number being assigned), `TZ_NUM_WAIT` (waiting for SMS), `TZ_NUM_ANSWER` (SMS arrived), `TZ_OVER_OK` (finished), `ERROR_NO_ITEMS` (failed). `msg` is absent until the first SMS. The server caches answers for a few seconds.

```ts
for (const op of await client.numbers.state({ orderBy: 'desc' })) {
  console.log(op.tzid, op.response, op.msg)
}
```

## stateOne

One operation.

```ts
stateOne(tzid: number, options?: { messageToCode?: boolean; msgList?: boolean }): Promise<Operation>
```

```ts
const op = await client.numbers.stateOne(tzid)
if (op.response === 'TZ_NUM_ANSWER') console.log(op.msg)
```

Errors: `ApiError` `ERROR_NO_OPERATIONS` when the operation does not exist (any more).

## waitCode

Poll the operation until a code arrives, then close it and return the code.

```ts
waitCode(tzid: number, options?: WaitCodeOptions): Promise<string>
```

| Option         | Type            | Default     | Description                                                          |
| -------------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `interval`     | `number`        | `5000`      | Poll interval, ms.                                                   |
| `timeout`      | `number`        | `600000`    | Give up after, ms.                                                   |
| `keepOpen`     | `boolean`       | `false`     | Call `next(tzid)` instead of `close(tzid)`, to wait for another SMS. |
| `fullMessage`  | `boolean`       | `false`     | Return the full SMS text instead of the code.                        |
| `since`        | `string | null` | `null`      | Ignore this value (the previous code).                               |
| `sleep`, `now` | functions       | real timers | Injectable for tests.                                                |

Transient errors are retried until the timeout: `TransportError`, and `ApiError` `TRY_AGAIN_LATER` (the HTTP 429 rate limit), `ERROR_UNDEFINED` and `INTERVAL_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_ERROR`. Any other `ApiError` is thrown at once.

```ts
const first = await client.numbers.waitCode(tzid, { keepOpen: true })
const second = await client.numbers.waitCode(tzid, { since: first })
```

Errors: `TimeoutError`; `ApiError` with code `TZ_OVER_OK` or `ERROR_NO_ITEMS` when the operation ended without a new code; any other `ApiError` from `stateOne`/`close`/`next`.

## next

Switch the operation to its next SMS and keep it open (for services that send several SMS).

```ts
next(tzid: number): Promise<true>
```

```ts
await client.numbers.next(tzid)
```

Errors: `ApiError` `ERROR_WRONG_TZID` (not an operation of your account), `ERROR_NO_TZID`.

## close

Finish the operation. An operation without SMS can be closed only after its guard interval (`guard_interval_remaining_seconds`); every attempt locks the tzid for 5 s.

```ts
close(tzid: number): Promise<true>
```

```ts
await client.numbers.close(tzid)
```

Errors: `ApiError` `NO_COMPLETE_TZID`, `INTERVAL_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_ERROR`, `ERROR_WRONG_TZID`.

## ban

Finish the operation and report the number as bad. Only before any SMS arrived.

```ts
ban(tzid: number): Promise<true>
```

```ts
await client.numbers.ban(tzid)
```

Errors: as `close`; `ApiError` with code `"0"` when the operation already has an SMS — nothing is changed then.

## tariffs

Services, prices and stock of every country, keyed by country code. No API key needed. The answer is large (a few MB); prefer `tariffsOne`.

```ts
tariffs(): Promise<Record<string, CountryStat>>
```

`CountryStat`: `{ name, locale_name?, position, code, other?, new, enabled, services }`; `services` maps `service_<slug>` to `{ count, popular, code, price, id, service, slug }`.

```ts
const all = await client.numbers.tariffs()
console.log(Object.keys(all).length, 'countries')
```

## tariffsOne

Services, prices and stock of one country.

```ts
tariffsOne(country = 7): Promise<CountryStat>
```

```ts
const uk = await client.numbers.tariffsOne(44)
for (const s of Object.values(uk.services)) console.log(s.slug, s.price, s.count)
```

Errors: `ApiError` `NO_COUNTRY`.


# Rent

A rent keeps a number for `days` days. Its SMS come in `RentItem.messages`, newest first.

`get` reserves the price (it shows in `zbalance`): the rent starts with `status` `0` and `checked` `false` and waits up to 20 minutes for its first SMS. The first SMS that is not a `notify` notice confirms it (`status` `1`) and charges the price; without one the rent closes and the reservation is released. Some countries (`confirm` in `tariffs`, e.g. US numbers) are confirmed and charged at once.

`RentItem`: `{ tzid, status, number, country, sum, days, hours, time, time_seconds?, extension, extend, messages, start_time, stop_time, day_extend?, … }` —
`sum` is the cost in USD incl. extensions (a number; `rent.state` gets it from the server as a decimal string), `time` minutes left, `time_seconds` seconds left,
`extension` `0` not extendable / `1` extendable / `2` auto-extension, `extend` maps days to the extension price (`{}` when not extendable),
`messages` is `RentSms[]`: `{ id, service, text, code, created_at }` — `code` is `''` when no code was found and the number `0` for a `notify` SMS (a prohibited sender).

## get

Rent a number. The price is reserved; the first SMS charges it.

```ts
get(country = 7, days = 1, extension = true): Promise<RentItem>
```

| Param       | Type      | Default | Description                                     |
| ----------- | --------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `country`   | `number`  | `7`     | Country code.                                   |
| `days`      | `number`  | `1`     | One of the tariff's `days` keys.                |
| `extension` | `boolean` | `true`  | `false` makes the rent non-extendable for good. |

```ts
const rent = await client.rent.get(7, 7)
console.log(rent.tzid, rent.number, rent.sum)
```

Errors: `NoNumberError`; `ApiError` `UNDEFINED_DAYS`, `UNDEFINED_COUNTRY`, `WARNING_LOW_BALANCE`, `INTERVAL_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_ERROR`, `TRY_AGAIN_LATER`.

## state

All rents of the account.

```ts
state(): Promise<RentItem[]>
```

```ts
for (const rent of await client.rent.state()) {
  console.log(rent.number, rent.messages[0]?.code)
}
```

## stateOne

One rent.

```ts
stateOne(tzid: number): Promise<RentItem>
```

```ts
const { messages } = await client.rent.stateOne(tzid)
```

Errors: `ApiError` `ERROR_NO_OPERATIONS` for an unknown tzid.

## extend

Extend a rent by `days` days and charge the balance at once. Only confirmed rents (`status` `1` or `4`) created with `extension: true`.

```ts
extend(tzid: number, days = 1): Promise<RentItem>
```

```ts
const rent = await client.rent.extend(tzid, 3)
console.log(rent.stop_time)
```

Errors: `ApiError` `TRY_AGAIN_LATER` (unknown tzid, not confirmed yet or closed, not extendable, unknown period, a repeat within 10 s), `WARNING_LOW_BALANCE`.

## close

Return the number before the period ends. A rent that is not confirmed yet (`status` `0`) and has no SMS can be closed only after 120 s; then, or with only `notify` SMS, the reservation is released. With a real SMS the rent is confirmed (charged) and closed. A confirmed rent closes without a refund. US numbers cannot be closed early.

```ts
close(tzid: number): Promise<true>
```

```ts
await client.rent.close(tzid)
```

Errors: `ApiError` `ERROR_NO_OPERATIONS`, `NO_COMPLETE_TZID`, `NO_CLOSE_RENT_US`, `TRY_AGAIN_LATER`.

## tariffs

Rent prices of every country, keyed by country code. No API key needed.

```ts
tariffs(): Promise<Record<string, RentTariff>>
```

`RentTariff`: `{ code, name, enabled, new, position, extend, confirm?, days, count, ext_counts? }` — `days` maps rent days to the price in USD, `count` to the numbers available.

```ts
const tariffs = await client.rent.tariffs()
```

## tariffsOne

Rent prices of one country.

```ts
tariffsOne(country = 7): Promise<RentTariff>
```

```ts
const { days } = await client.rent.tariffsOne(7)
console.log(days['7']) // price of 7 days
```

Errors: `ApiError` `NO_COUNTRY` for a country without rent.


# Testing

`MockOnlineSim` is an in-process fake of the OnlineSim API that ships with the package. It is a `fetch` implementation that answers like the real backend — same shapes, same error codes, HTTP 456 for a wrong key — and keeps a balance, operations and rents. Your code talks to a normal `OnlineSim` client, so nothing in it changes for tests. It is deterministic: no randomness, no clock, numbers and ids come from a counter.

## Setup

```ts
import { MockOnlineSim } from 'onlinesim-js-api'

const mock = new MockOnlineSim({ balance: 10 })
const client = mock.client() // an OnlineSim wired to the mock
```

```ts
new MockOnlineSim(options?: {
  apiKey?: string        // default 'mock-key'
  balance?: number       // USD, default 100
  prices?: Record<number, Record<string, number>>                                 // country → service → USD
  rentTariffs?: Record<number, { days: Record<number, number>; extend: number }>  // country → tariff
  guardInterval?: number // seconds, default 0
})
```

| Option          | Default                                                                               | Description                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apiKey`        | `'mock-key'`                                                                          | Key the mock accepts. `mock.client()` uses it; `mock.client({ apiKey: 'x' })` tests a wrong key.                |
| `balance`       | `100`                                                                                 | Starting balance, USD.                                                                                          |
| `prices`        | `{ 7: { vkcom: 0.5, telegram: 1.2, google: 0.3 }, 44: { google: 0.2, vkcom: 0.36 } }` | Number prices; replaces the defaults. Also feeds `numbers.tariffs()`.                                           |
| `rentTariffs`   | `{ 7: { days: { 1: 1, 3: 2.5, 7: 5 }, extend: 1 } }`                                  | Rent prices; `extend: 0` makes rents of that country non-extendable.                                            |
| `guardInterval` | `0`                                                                                   | `> 0`: an operation without SMS, or an unconfirmed rent without any SMS, cannot be closed (`NO_COMPLETE_TZID`). |

`mock.client(options?)` takes the usual [client options](https://s00d.github.io/onlinesim-js-api/#client-options) except `fetch`. To build the client yourself, pass `mock.transport` as `fetch`; any `baseUrl` works:

```ts
import { MockOnlineSim, OnlineSim } from 'onlinesim-js-api'

const mock = new MockOnlineSim()
const client = new OnlineSim({ apiKey: 'mock-key', fetch: mock.transport })
```

## A full example

Order a number, let an SMS arrive while `waitCode` polls, check the code and the money. `addSmsAfter` delivers the SMS after a number of polls instead of after some time, so `waitCode` runs with `interval: 0` and the test takes milliseconds.

```ts
import { expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { MockOnlineSim } from 'onlinesim-js-api'

it('receives the code', async () => {
  const mock = new MockOnlineSim({ balance: 10 })
  const client = mock.client()

  const { tzid, number } = await client.numbers.getWithNumber('google', 44)
  expect(number).toBe('+44900000001')

  mock.addSmsAfter(tzid, 'Your Google code: 123-456', 2) // the third poll sees it
  const code = await client.numbers.waitCode(tzid, { interval: 0 })

  expect(code).toBe('123456')
  expect(mock.operations()[0]?.status).toBe('TZ_OVER_OK') // waitCode closed it
  expect(mock.balance()).toBe(9.8) // the price is spent once an SMS arrived
})
```

The `msg` of an operation is the code by default: the first run of 4–8 digits, with spaces and dashes between digits removed (`123-456` → `123456`); a text without such a run comes back whole. `messageToCode: false` (or `fullMessage` in `waitCode`) gives the full text.

## Errors

`failNext(code)` makes the next request answer `{"response": code}` — the client turns it into `ApiError` (or `NoNumberError`) exactly as for the real server. Pass `endpoint` to fail only that endpoint. `failNextTransport()` makes the next request fail with a non-JSON HTTP 502 (`TransportError`).

```ts
import { expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { MockOnlineSim, NoNumberError, TransportError } from 'onlinesim-js-api'

it('handles a missing number and a network hiccup', async () => {
  const mock = new MockOnlineSim()
  const client = mock.client()

  mock.failNext('NO_NUMBER', { endpoint: 'getNum.php' })
  await expect(client.numbers.get('google')).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(NoNumberError)

  mock.failNextTransport({ status: 503 })
  await expect(client.user.balance()).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(TransportError)

  await expect(client.user.balance()).resolves.toMatchObject({ balance: 100 }) // one-shot
})
```

The state itself produces the real error codes too: `WARNING_LOW_BALANCE` when the balance is short, `NO_NUMBER` when `reject` matches the next number, `UNDEFINED_COUNTRY` / `ERROR_NO_SERVICE` for unknown prices, `ERROR_WRONG_TZID` for an unknown or closed operation (`next` too; `ERROR_NO_TZID` for tzid `0`), `UNDEFINED_COUNTRY` / `UNDEFINED_DAYS` for an unknown rent country or period, `TRY_AGAIN_LATER` for every refused `rent.extend`, `ERROR_NO_OPERATIONS` for an unknown rent in `rent.close`, `ERROR_WRONG_KEY` for a wrong key (HTTP 456) or no key (HTTP 200).

## Inspecting requests

`mock.requests` lists every request received: `{ method, path, query, body }`, `path` relative to `/api/`.

```ts
import { expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { MockOnlineSim } from 'onlinesim-js-api'

it('sends reject as a comma list', async () => {
  const mock = new MockOnlineSim()
  await mock.client().numbers.get('google', 44, { reject: ['4470', '4471'] })

  expect(mock.requests).toEqual([
    { method: 'GET', path: 'getNum.php', query: { service: 'google', country: '44', reject: '4470,4471', lang: 'en' }, body: undefined },
  ])
})
```

## Control API

| Member                                         | Description                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `client(options?)`                             | A normal `OnlineSim` wired to the mock.                                                                             |
| `transport`                                    | The fake `fetch`.                                                                                                   |
| `addSms(tzid, text, { service? })`             | An SMS arrives now at a number operation or a rent (detected by `tzid`). Throws for an unknown or closed one.       |
| `addSmsAfter(tzid, text, polls, { service? })` | The SMS arrives after `polls` state requests for `tzid` (`numbers.state`/`stateOne`, `rent.state`/`stateOne`).      |
| `failNext(code, { endpoint? })`                | The next request (to `endpoint` only, e.g. `'getNum.php'`) answers `{"response": code}`.                            |
| `failNextTransport({ status?, endpoint? })`    | The next request fails with a non-JSON body and HTTP `status` (default `502`).                                      |
| `setBalance(usd)` / `balance()`                | Set / read the total balance, USD (it includes the part frozen by open operations, as `user.balance()` reports it). |
| `operations()` / `rents()`                     | Copies of the current number operations / open rents, for assertions.                                               |
| `requests`                                     | Log of the requests received.                                                                                       |
| `reset()`                                      | Back to the constructor's state.                                                                                    |

## What the mock does

- **Numbers**: `get` freezes the price; `close` after an SMS spends it, `close` without one refunds it; `ban` after an SMS answers `"0"`, like the server. Numbers are `+<country>9000000NN`, ids count from 1. `next` switches to the following SMS. The operation's `time` stays at 1200 s — there is no clock.
- **Rent**: `get` reserves the price (`status` `0`, `checked` `false`) and keeps the `extension` flag; the first SMS that is not `notify` confirms the rent (`status` `1`) and charges it — `addSms(tzid, text, { service: 'notify' })` adds a notice with `code` `0` that confirms nothing. `extend` works on a confirmed rent and charges at once. `close` releases the reservation of an unconfirmed rent and gives no refund for a confirmed one. `sum` is a number in `get`/`extend` and a decimal string on the wire of `state`, like the server. SMS appear in `messages`, newest first.
- **User**: `balance` (frozen part included), a fixed profile, `setWebhookUrl` accepts any `scheme://…` URL (`VALIDATION_ERROR` otherwise), `webhookLogs` lists the deliveries the mock *recorded* when an SMS arrived while a webhook URL was set — it makes no HTTP call; their `params` follow the real payload (`code` `''` without a code, rent `number` in digits without `+`, rent `time_left` in minutes). `paymentHistory` has no orders.
- **Free**: `free.list` returns two fixed countries (44 first) with one number and a few SMS each.
- Not imitated: anything that needs real time — the 5 s lock after `setOperationOk` (`INTERVAL_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_ERROR`), the 10 s lock of `rent.extend`, the 120 s before an unconfirmed rent may be closed and its 20-minute wait for the first SMS. `guardInterval > 0` stands in for "too early to close".


# User

## balance

Balance in USD.

```ts
balance(): Promise<{ balance: number; zbalance: number; income?: number }>
```

`balance` includes the sum frozen by numbers and unconfirmed rents in progress (`zbalance`, which may be negative): available = `balance − max(zbalance, 0)`. `income` is the partner income. The server caches the answer for 60 s.

```ts
const { balance, zbalance } = await client.user.balance()
const available = balance - Math.max(zbalance, 0)
```

Errors: `ApiError` `ERROR_WRONG_KEY`, `ACCOUNT_BLOCKED`, `API_ACCESS_DISABLED`, `API_ACCESS_IP`.

## profile

The account profile.

```ts
profile(): Promise<Profile>
```

`Profile`: `{ id, name, username, email, locale, currency, number_country, number_reject, webhook_url, api_access, … }`.

```ts
const { email, webhook_url } = await client.user.profile()
```

## paymentHistory

Top-up orders (paginated, newest first) and the available payment methods.

```ts
paymentHistory(page = 1): Promise<PaymentHistory>
```

`PaymentHistory`: `{ orders: Paginator<PaymentOrder>, paylist, domains?, forms?, currency?, buttons? }`. `PaymentOrder.sum` stays a decimal string (`"89.00"`); `currency` and `form_text` may be `null`. `paylist` maps a group id to its payment methods, or is a list when the ids are 0, 1, 2… (the server sends a JSON array then).

```ts
const { orders } = await client.user.paymentHistory()
console.log(`${orders.total} orders, page ${orders.current_page}/${orders.last_page}`)
```

## setWebhookUrl

Set the URL that receives SMS webhooks (see [Webhooks](https://s00d.github.io/onlinesim-js-api/webhooks)).

```ts
setWebhookUrl(url: string): Promise<true>
```

```ts
await client.user.setWebhookUrl('https://example.com/onlinesim-hook')
```

Errors: `ApiError` `VALIDATION_ERROR` for an invalid URL; `message` holds the server's field messages.

## clearWebhookUrl

Remove the webhook URL, also from operations in progress.

```ts
clearWebhookUrl(): Promise<true>
```

```ts
await client.user.clearWebhookUrl()
```

## webhookLogs

Webhook delivery log, newest first, 10 per page.

```ts
webhookLogs(page = 1): Promise<Paginator<WebhookLog>>
```

`WebhookLog`: `{ id, user_id, webhook_url, type, params, status, error, created_at, updated_at }` — `type` is `receiving_sms` or `rent_sms`, `status` is `success`, `fail` or `pending`, `params` the payload that was sent.

```ts
const logs = await client.user.webhookLogs()
for (const log of logs.data) console.log(log.created_at, log.status, log.error)
```


# Webhooks

Set a URL with [`client.user.setWebhookUrl`](https://s00d.github.io/onlinesim-js-api/user#setwebhookurl). For each SMS the server POSTs a JSON body to it: `webhook_type` `receiving_sms` for numbers, `rent_sms` for rents. Delivery attempts are listed by [`client.user.webhookLogs`](https://s00d.github.io/onlinesim-js-api/user#webhooklogs).

## parseWebhook

Parse an inbound webhook body from a JSON string or an already parsed object.

```ts
parseWebhook(payload: string | Record<string, unknown>): WebhookPayload
```

Lenient: numeric fields may arrive as strings, missing or malformed fields become `null`, unknown fields are dropped. It throws `OnlineSimError` only when the input is not a JSON object.

```ts
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { parseWebhook } from 'onlinesim-js-api'

createServer((req, res) => {
  let body = ''
  req.on('data', (chunk) => (body += chunk))
  req.on('end', () => {
    const hook = parseWebhook(body)
    if (hook.webhook_type === 'receiving_sms') console.log(hook.operation_id, hook.code)
    res.end('ok')
  })
}).listen(8080)
```

## Payload fields

| Field          | Type                                  | Description                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `webhook_type` | `'receiving_sms' | 'rent_sms' | null` | Kind of operation.                                                                                                           |
| `operation_id` | `number | null`                       | `tzid` of the operation or rent.                                                                                             |
| `user_id`      | `number | null`                       | Account id.                                                                                                                  |
| `country_code` | `number | null`                       | Country code of the number.                                                                                                  |
| `number`       | `string | null`                       | Numbers: `+` and the full number (`+79001234567`), or `hidden`. Rent: the full number in digits without `+` (`79001234567`). |
| `sender`       | `string | null`                       | Sender of the SMS, e.g. `VK`.                                                                                                |
| `message`      | `string | null`                       | Full SMS text.                                                                                                               |
| `code`         | `string | null`                       | Code extracted from the SMS; `''` when none was found.                                                                       |
| `time_start`   | `string | null`                       | Numbers: when the operation was ordered. Rent: when the SMS arrived. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.                                  |
| `time_left`    | `number | null`                       | Time left: seconds for numbers, minutes for rent.                                                                            |
